The '''2016–17 Eredivisie''' season was the 61st season of the top-tier Dutch League [[Eredivisie]] since its establishment in 1956. The fixtures for this season were announced on 14 June 2016.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.eredivisie.nl/nieuwsbericht/eredivisieseizoen-trapt-af-in-nijmegen |title=EREDIVISIESEIZOEN BEGINT IN NIJMEGEN |website=www.eredivisie.nl |date=14 June 2016 |access-date=14 June 2016 |archive-date=10 October 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161010153510/http://www.eredivisie.nl/nieuwsbericht/eredivisieseizoen-trapt-af-in-nijmegen |url-status=dead }}</ref> [[PSV Eindhoven|PSV]] were the defending champions after winning the title for a record [[2015–16 Eredivisie|23rd]] time. 

At the end of the season, [[Feyenoord]] became the title-holders for a record 15th time and the first since the [[1998–99 Eredivisie|1998–99]] season.

== Teams ==
A total of 18 teams took part in the league: The best fifteen teams from the [[2015–16 Eredivisie|2015–16 season]], two promotion/relegation playoff winners and the [[2015–16 Eerste Divisie]] champions.

[[Sparta Rotterdam]], the champion of the 2015–16 Eerste Divisie, returned to the Eredivisie after spending six seasons in the Eerste Divisie, whereas play-off winner [[Go Ahead Eagles]] returned to the Eredivisie after just one season. They replaced relegated teams [[SC Cambuur|Cambuur]] and [[De Graafschap]].

As a result of financial maladministration, the [[Royal Dutch Football Association|KNVB]] had originally taken [[FC Twente]]'s license, causing them to relegate to the [[2016-17 Eerste Divisie]]. However, FC Twente successfully appealed this decision and was therefore allowed to stay in the league.<ref>{{cite web|title=Beroepscommissie: FC Twente behoudt licentie en krijgt boete van 181.000 euro|url=http://www.knvb.nl/nieuws/betaald-voetbal/licenties/18882/beroepscommissie-fc-twente-behoudt-licentie-en-krijgt-boete|website=knvb.nl|publisher=[[Royal Dutch Football Association]]|access-date=17 June 2016|language=nl}}</ref>

=== Promotion/relegation play-offs ===
Ten teams, two (NEC and Roda JC, as 16th- and 17th-placed teams) from the Eredivisie and eight from the [[2016–17 Eerste Divisie|Eerste Divisie]], played for two spots in the [[2017–18 Eredivisie]], the remaining eight teams play in the [[2017–18 Eerste Divisie]].
